title: Tony Robbins and Dean Graziosi FAKE GURU Course
summary: Critique of a high-ticket course launch: affiliate-only reviews, low completion rates, no disqualification of buyers, hype seminars over results, far cheaper alternatives exist.

assertions.quote: there is a much better product available for people at a much more affordable price
these affiliate marketers only get paid when you purchase the course the review is about as honest as steroid era baseball players

verdicts.note: Empire paid an affiliate over $1.5 million in commissions to post sales results and tout his success on social media even though his own Empire-managed store was unprofitable and suspended; paid promotion, not reviews as such.

assertions.quote: only about 10 to 15 percent of customers even complete the course

verdicts.note: Online course completion rates are commonly reported in the 5 to 15 percent range, though paid cohorts do better.

assertions.quote: very few people are going to make their money back this course is promoted as a way to own your future

verdicts.note: For Automators' coaching and automation packages the FTC alleges most buyers did not recoup their investment and virtually none earned the advertised amounts; DK Automation and Nudge show the same pattern, though all are enforcement cases rather than a survey of courses generally.

assertions.quote: these people will find out that their expertise in petting their dog isn't something that generates sales

verdicts.note: Course marketplaces show a long tail where most courses sell few or no copies.

assertions.quote: these kinds of courses rely on people purchasing the course who aren't a good fit

verdicts.note: Funnels rarely screen buyers, but whether the business model requires unfit buyers is not established.

assertions.quote: information is about two to five percent of success implementing and navigating setbacks is the remaining ninety-five percent

verdicts.note: A framing about what drives success, not a measurable split.

assertions.quote: the easiest thing in sales is selling a product that works

verdicts.note: An inference about marketing spend, not directly testable.

assertions.quote: the money is in selling success not attaining it through building an actual business
